title: Documentation: module docs, security note, doc-tests
description:
Write all documentation for the uuencoding crate. This is a deliverable, not an afterthought.

Required:
1. Crate-level doc (src/lib.rs):
   - What UUencoding is and where it came from (pre-MIME, UUCP/Usenet era)
   - The two use cases: CTE-declared (Content-Transfer-Encoding: x-uuencode in a MIME part) and inline (begin/end block embedded in text/plain body)
   - How this crate fits with mime-tree (mime-tree depends on this; this crate does not depend on mime-tree)
   - Quick-start examples for decode(), encode(), and scan()
   - Security note: decoded output can be significantly larger than encoded input. If the decoded bytes are themselves a compressed archive, any decompression is the caller's responsibility and must be independently guarded against decompression bombs. This crate does not decompress anything.

2. Each public type: full doc comment on the struct and every field.

3. Each public function: doc comment covering parameters, return value, error conditions, and at least one doc-test that compiles and passes.

4. UuError variants: each variant's doc must explain when it is produced and what the caller should do.

5. The begin-base64 note: document that begin-base64 is a different encoding (MIME base64 in disguise) and that callers who receive BeginBase64 should pass the block to a standard base64 decoder instead.

6. A prominent note that the crate tolerates real-world 'trash': CRLF line endings, trailing-space stripping by mailers, space/backtick ambiguity, and missing end lines. Callers do not need to pre-sanitize input.

All doc-tests must use oracle-derived expected values (Python uu module or UNIX uuencode), not values derived from this crate.
